name: WA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 10 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Emily Randall has a massive fundraising edge ($1.2M vs $28K)
Prediction markets price Randall at 99% to win
model.rationale: Randall combines a solidly Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial advantage over Teresa Fox, while markets price her near-certain. With no contrary polling or outside spending, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 21 points stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much closer race or significant outside spending against Randall would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Emily Randall defends a western Washington seat that leans Democratic by about ten points. She has raised roughly $1.2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Teresa Fox has raised under $30,000 with no outside support on either side. No independent groups are opposing Randall, and prediction markets price her at about 99 percent to win.

No general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Those point to a comfortable double-digit win for Randall, with uncertainty driven mainly by the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
